Title: Touted as Waze alternative, TuJu now redirects users to Google Maps
Article:
New Straits Times
KUALA LUMPUR: TuJu users are now being redirected to Google Maps when they tap the navigation button.
This comes following the app's latest update amid efforts to resolve navigation disruptions.
The Android update, version 2.0.4, released on Oct 30, replaces TuJu's in-app navigation with Google Maps.
A New Straits Times test found that tapping "Navigation" prompted a pop-up informing users that Google Maps would open to continue their journey.
The existing iOS version also redirects users to Google Maps, although it remains listed as version 1.5.5, last updated in November 2025.
On Oct 21, the government
banned civil servants
from using Waze, citing the app's Israeli origins, prompting the promotion of TuJu as an alternative navigation app.
The app experienced disruptions a day after the government announced plans to switch to TuJu as an alternative to Waze.
TuJu later
apologised for navigation disruptions,
saying restoration work was expected to be completed by Nov 6.
Its developer, Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd, said its technical team was carrying out recovery and improvement work to ensure its features operated smoothly and reliably.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Status won't protect domestic violence perpetrators, says Penang exco member
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A person's social status, background or public standing will not protect him or her from action against domestic violence.
Social Development, Welfare and Non-Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Lim Siew Khim said no one was above the law.
"Domestic violence does not discriminate based on position, title, or social status.
"Whether an individual is an ordinary member of the public, a public figure, or an elected representative, everyone is equally accountable under the law," she said in a statement in response to allegations of domestic violence involving a Penang assemblyman.
Lim, however, said police must first be allowed to conduct a thorough investigation into the matter without interference.
"At this stage, it would be inappropriate to draw conclusions or make judgments against any party before the facts have been established.
"If any wrongdoing is proven, the necessary action must be taken in accordance with the law," she said, cautioning against the spread of unverified information.
Yesterday, police said they recorded statements from four people, including a Penang assemblyman and his wife, over an
alleged domestic assault
involving the couple.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim had confirmed that a police report was lodged and investigations were ongoing under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which concerns voluntarily causing hurt
Lim said the case serves as a stark reminder that domestic abuse remains a pressing societal concern requiring ongoing vigilance and comprehensive victim-support mechanisms.
She said the Penang government continues to tackle domestic abuse through initiatives like the Safe Family Policy, rolled out in 2020 in partnership with the Women's Centre for Change (WCC) and Penang Women's Development Corporation (PWDC).
Under the initiative, frontline personnel across state constituency service centres, government departments, and non-governmental organisations are trained as First Support Points (FSPs) to assist victims.
To date, 536 community members and organisational representatives have been trained under the network.
The state has also introduced the "Penang Stop Violence" mobile app to help survivors locate the nearest FSP and access emergency guidance.
"Victims of domestic violence should never feel that they have nowhere to turn. We want to ensure that anyone facing violence knows that support, protection, and assistance are available, regardless of their circumstances," Lim said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jais tracking owners of Puchong warehouse in 6.5-tonne halal chicken probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor Islamic Religious Affairs Department (Jais) is tracking down the owners of a Puchong warehouse where more than 6.5 tonnes of
raw chicken
were seized over halal violations.
Its director, Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad, said Jais was working with the District and Land Office to obtain details on the registered company and the actual owners of the premises.
Jais' investigations found that the premises had no proper signage, halal certification application records or a Halal Certification Certificate.
Shahzihan said the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) had never issued slaughterer certification for activities at the site.
"Our records also indicate that operations at the premises were carried out by more than one company or entity," he said.
In the Oct 30 raid, 12 Bangladeshi and Pakistani men, believed to be workers at the facility, were arrested.
It was later found that the chickens had been electrocuted before being slaughtered.
Shahzihan said Jais was investigating the case under Section 4(1) of the Trade (Halal Definition) Act and Section 121F of the Islamic Religious Administration (Selangor) Enactment.
The sections cover passing off items as halal without meeting the requirements and carrying out halal slaughtering without a valid certificate. The offences carry jail terms and fines.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib fundraising drive still short of target, says Umno sec-gen
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Public donations to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak continue to come in, although the fundraising drive has yet to reach its target to cover his fine.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said daily collections averaged between RM5,000 and RM10,000.
He said contributions had come from people across all walks of life, including those who donated as little as RM1, RM5 and RM10.
"The momentum is good. I have observed that daily contributions from the public average between RM5,000 and RM10,000, including donations as small as RM10, RM5 and even RM1.
"This is what we call crowdfunding, where members of the public contribute to help Najib," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the Program Santai Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki bersama pengundi at the Durian Tunggal state constituency operations room in Taman Angkasa Nuri here today.
Also present were BN candidate for the Durian Tunggal seat Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa and former assemblyman Datuk Zahari Khalil.
Asyraf Wajdi said the fundraising effort was still ongoing, but the total amount collected had yet to be disclosed as the party wanted to wait for an appropriate time to announce it.
"God willing, I am confident, but I want to keep an element of surprise. We will make the announcement when the time comes," he said.
On political opponents continuing to raise Najib's name during the Melaka election campaign, Asyraf Wajdi said he believed the public still remembered the former prime minister's administration, particularly its impact on people's lives and the country's economy.
It was  previously reported that Najib had yet to pay the RM50 million fine, based on the latest information from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said no specific deadline had been set for payment of the fine and confirmed that Najib would have to remain in prison until it was paid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rayer: Why hasn't Zakir Naik been extradited, who pays for apartment, bodyguards?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) has questioned why the government will not extradite preacher Dr Zakir Naik to India.
"I would like to ask why. He is someone who has stirred up various controversies," he said in the Dewan Rakyat here while debating the 2027 Supply Bill at the committee stage.
He said he understood that Zakir lived in a luxury apartment in Putrajaya and asked who bore the cost.
"I also understand that whenever he goes out for any event, personal bodyguards are provided.
"Who bears the cost of his bodyguards? Does the government bear the cost?"
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had said earlier that the government had decided
not to extradite Zakir
and had made no commitment to hand him over to India.
Rayer recalled that Zakir gave a speech in Kota Baru on Aug 8, 2019, questioning the loyalty of Malaysian citizens of Indian and Chinese descent.
"This angered Malaysian citizens of Indian and Chinese descent, and police reports were lodged," he said.
Rayer's debate was interrupted by Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik), who said Zakir was outside the Dewan Rakyat and could not respond.
"I am not giving way... this is my time. I do not want to be interrupted," Rayer replied.
Deputy Speaker Alice Lau told Tarmizi to sit down and not interrupt.
Rayer then repeated his question to the government.
"So, I ask the government for an explanation, and I want to know why he is not being sent back to India," he said.
Earlier, Saifuddin said the decision was based on Malaysia's rights under Article 6 of the extradition treaty signed with the Indian government in 2010, as well as provisions under the Extradition Act 1992.
He said the government had not received any new extradition request from India concerning Zakir.
The Indian government had submitted an official extradition request on Jan 19, 2018, followed by a diplomatic note seeking a review of the decision on May 29, 2020.
The calls for clarification over Zakir's extradition followed media reports that the matter, sought by India over allegations of money laundering and hate speech, was discussed in talks between Anwar and Indian representatives.
Indian news outlet New Delhi Television (NDTV) reported that Anwar had confirmed the matter was discussed behind closed doors, in New Delhi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SP Setia unit, Help seal deal for Kinrara International School
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SP Setia Bhd's unit Perumahan Kinrara Bhd and Help Kinrara Sdn Bhd have signed a build-and-lease agreement for a new international school in Bandar Kinrara.
SP Setia will develop the purpose-built campus, and Help will lease and operate it as the fourth school in the group, targeted to open in August 2029.
The international school will be developed on a 0.81-hectare site within the 6.45-hectare commercial land parcel in Bandar Kinrara.
It is planned as a six-storey campus with an indicative gross floor area of 176,085 square feet and capacity for more than 1,000 students.
The international school intends to serve families in Bandar Kinrara and surrounding communities while contributing to a more integrated, accessible and liveable urban precinct.
It is expected to offer primary and secondary programmes based on the British Curriculum, incorporating the International Primary Curriculum and leading to Cambridge IGCSE qualifications, for students aged five to 16.
The campus is planned to include 55 classrooms, six science laboratories with preparation rooms, an engineering and design workshop, a food technology kitchen, two music rooms, two art rooms, dedicated edtech facilities, a library of about 4,200 square feet and a multipurpose hall that spans 6,000 square feet.
Under the agreements, Perumahan Kinrara will undertake the development and construction of the school complex.
Help will secure the required education approvals and complete the campus fit-out before the school opens.
"Setia's collaboration with Help reflects this approach to innovation, bringing complementary expertise into our townships to create places that offer more than a home.
"By integrating education into the wider vision for Bandar Kinrara, we aim to enhance everyday living for existing homeowners and give prospective buyers greater confidence in the community they choose to be part of," SP Setia president and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Zaini Yusoff said in a statement.
"Beyond academic achievement, at the heart of every Help school is a commitment to nurturing the whole child and equipping them to be career and future ready for a fast-changing world.
"This commitment is reflected in our accreditation by the Council of International Schools, a testament to the care our leaders, teachers and staff bring to our schools every day," said Help Group co-CEO Dr Gerard Louis.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil society groups demand cross-party deal on eight key reforms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A coalition of civil society organisations (CSOs) wants the government and opposition to sign a cross-party agreement involving all 218 members of parliament.
This, they said, was to execute eight key institutional reforms before the end of the 15th Parliament's term.
They said that without such an agreement, key reforms may be held back by political uncertainties and may be susceptible to unelected forces that do not want these reforms to empower Malaysian voters.
"This agreement should aim to pave the way for the consolidation of parliamentary democracy before and after the 16th General Election and to restore public and international confidence in political stability and accountability in Malaysia.
"It must therefore cover concerns of both the Madani government and Perikatan Nasional," they said in a statement.
They also want Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to reach out directly to PN's top leadership to deepen democracy and enhance stability.
"As (Anwar) enters the last year of his term, this is his moment as a statesman to unite all parties to introduce far-reaching changes.
"It is equally a golden opportunity for PN to propose a comprehensive deal to the government, to show its visionary leadership and democratic commitment for Malaysia after GE16."
Among the eight reforms are limiting a prime minister's term to 10 years; separation of the powers of the attorney-general and the public prosecutor; a Freedom of Information Act; an Ombudsman Act; an Equitable Constituency Development Fund (CDF) Act; and, a Political Financing Act with public funding for political parties.
The others are that the Election Commission be made answerable to Parliament and not the prime minister and that a three-month notice for parliamentary dissolution if there is no agreement for the 15th Parliament to serve its full term till Dec 18, 2027.
The CSOs said Anwar should keep to the promise he made at the beginning of his term, as the first two reforms require a two-thirds majority (148 votes) to amend the Federal Constitution.
"The PM's 10-year tenure limit would enable leadership renewal and rejuvenation and prevent power abuse and dynastic politics. The AG-PP separation is necessary to prevent selective prosecution, selective impunity and a two-tiered society."
The Freedom of Information and Ombudsman acts, said the CSOs, would empower ordinary Malaysians, enhance transparency, and motivate civil servants to deliver better public services.
The group noted these reforms might face resistance, but urged any party seeking to form the next government to deliver them within the current term.
They added that the four other reforms are vital to ensure a level playing field for both the government and the opposition.
"Equitable CDF should be accessible to all MPs and assemblymen without being monopolised or made conditional on government support," the group said.
As for the Political Finance Act, they said this would prevent money politics and foreign interference.
Among the 33 CSOs are Aliran, G25 Malaysia, the Centre for Independent Journalism (CIJ) and the National Human Rights Society.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB accelerates grid modernisation to meet rising current, future demand: CEO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) is stepping up investments in grid infrastructure and accelerating network modernisation to strengthen Malaysia's electricity supply system, enhance renewable energy integration and meet future demand.
It's president and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Shamsul Ahmad said forward planning, faster project execution and stronger collaboration were essential to developing a smarter, more flexible and resilient national grid.
Speaking during the "The Grid of Tomorrow" panel at Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026, he said TNB was investing ahead of demand while balancing the need for affordable, sustainable and reliable electricity supply.
The utility serves approximately 11 million customers and has allocated about RM43 billion for network investments under Regulatory Period 4 (RP4), covering 2025 to 2027.
He said the investments would support the development of critical infrastructure, including the 500-kilovolt (kV) National Grid Backbone, targeted for completion by 2030, and the 100-megawatt (MW)/400-megawatt-hour (MWh) Santong Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Terengganu.
TNB began developing the National Grid Backbone in August 2026, with the approximately 500-kilometre transmission system designed to connect strategic locations along the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia. Upon completion, it will be the country's longest 500kV transmission system, strengthening grid capacity, flexibility and reliability.
Meanwhile, the Santong BESS, which commenced operations in April 2026, is Malaysia's first grid-connected battery energy storage system. Located in Dungun, Terengganu, it can deliver 100 MW of power for up to four hours, providing additional flexibility to manage electricity supply and support the integration of renewable energy sources.
At the regional level, Shamsul highlighted the growing momentum behind the Asean Power Grid (APG), supported by initiatives such as the Laos-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore Power Integration Project (LTMS-PIP) and bilateral electricity trading arrangements between Malaysia and Singapore.
The LTMS-PIP, which began in June 2022, marked the first multilateral cross-border electricity trade involving four ASEAN countries, enabling renewable hydropower from Laos to be transmitted to Singapore through Thailand and Malaysia.
Its subsequent expansion has facilitated greater electricity trading, including supply from Malaysia to Singapore.
Malaysia and Singapore are also pursuing a second electricity interconnection between Peninsular Malaysia and Singapore, with a potential capacity of up to 2,000 MW.
TNB, Singapore's SP Group and Singapore Energy Interconnections signed a joint development agreement in October 2025 to undertake a full feasibility study for the proposed link, targeted to commence operations by 2030.
Shamsul said closer coordination among Asean governments, utilities and regulators, alongside aligned policies, regulatory frameworks and technical standards, would be crucial to translating regional ambitions into an interconnected and resilient electricity network.
The Asean Power Grid is aimed at connecting the electricity systems of member states to facilitate cross-border electricity trade, strengthen regional energy security and support the integration of renewable energy.
Malaysia's National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), launched in July 2023, provides the broader policy framework for the country's energy transition, covering six key areas: energy efficiency, renewable energy, hydrogen, bioenergy, green mobility and carbon capture, utilisation and storage.
SIEW is an annual, high-level platform for energy professionals, policymakers, and commentators to discuss and share best practices within the global energy space.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: BN-PN cooperation goes beyond paper, machinery work together
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) machinery in the Melaka election has improved, with both sides increasingly working together on the campaign trail.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the development was a good sign for BN and its candidates.
He said the cooperation was better than during the Negri Sembilan election, when the machinery of both coalitions campaigned separately.
He said this was evident in Melaka, where BN and PN campaign machinery had been attending campaign programmes together, particularly night ceramah.
"PN machinery has been helping in areas contested by BN, while BN machinery has also been instructed to give full support in areas contested by PN.
"Usually, at night, we can see representatives of the campaign machinery, voters and supporters, regardless of party affiliation, particularly from BN and PN, coming together.
"In areas contested by BN, we can see PN machinery lending a hand. Likewise, the leadership and I have instructed BN machinery in areas contested by PN to give their full support," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the Program Santai Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki bersama pengundi at the operations room for the Durian Tunggal state constituency in Taman Angkasa Nuri here today.
Also present were BN candidate for the Durian Tunggal seat Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa and former Durian Tunggal assemblyman Datuk Zahari Khalil.
Asyraf Wajdi said BN's campaign in Melaka had been more subdued, with the focus on its performance and service record rather than attacks against political opponents.
He said the people could assess for themselves the performance of caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh's administration, as well as the service delivered by the 21 BN assemblymen who were given the mandate in the previous election.
He added that some Pakatan Harapan candidates had even acknowledged that BN's administrative performance was difficult to criticise.
Asyraf Wajdi said the people of Melaka wanted a responsible government and hoped those elected would emulate previous leaders who had served the people regardless of race.
He also reminded party machinery to campaign responsibly and refrain from insulting, disparaging, slandering or making baseless allegations against their opponents throughout the campaign period.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Proton closes in on 200,000-unit sales milestone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Proton Holdings Bhd is closing in on its first 200,000-unit annual sales milestone since 2002.
The national carmaker recorded 182,510 vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, already surpassing its full-year sales volume for 2025.
Proton sold 21,624 units in October, its second-highest monthly sales performance this year and the strongest start to the fourth quarter since 2005.
Year-to-date (YTD) sales rose 40.5 per cent year-on-year, giving Proton an estimated market share of 27.1 per cent.
Its October market share was estimated at 30.6 per cent, against an estimated total industry volume (TIV) of more than 70,000 units.
Deputy chief executive officer Datuk Ir Abdul Rashid Musa said 2026 was shaping up to be a year of significant sales growth as the group pursued its long-term ambitions.
"2026 is proving to be a year where Proton makes a quantum leap in sales volume as we strive to achieve our long-term goals.
"While we continue to expand our range of xEV offerings, demand for Proton ICE (internal combustion engine) models continues to grow and as a result, we are the market leader for SUV sales and the leading brand for sedan sales," he said.
Proton Saga remains the company's biggest-selling model, with 7,352 units sold in October, bringing its YTD total to 75,589 units.
This has already exceeded the model's entire 2025 sales volume, keeping it Malaysia's second best-selling vehicle this year.
Proton S70 recorded 3,029 units in October, its second-best monthly performance this year, taking YTD sales to 23,448 units, up 63.5 per cent.
Meanwhile, the newly launched 2027 S70 i-GT 1.5 sold 2,338 units in October, making it the leading B-segment sedan, while the existing S70 retained its C-segment leadership.
Proton X50 remained the country's leading B-segment sport utility vehicle with 1,925 units sold in October and YTD sales of 22,088 units.
The X90 posted its best monthly performance with 478 units, taking YTD sales to 3,728 units, up 75.6 per cent.
Proton's electrified vehicle (xEV) range also continued to drive growth, with the e.Mas brand recording 35,730 units in YTD sales and a 33.2 per cent share of the xEV market.
The e.Mas 5 contributed 23,189 units, followed by the e.Mas 7 plug-in hybrid electric vehicle at 6,962 units and e.Mas 7 at 5,579 units.
Pro-Net chief executive officer Zhang Qiang said growing brand confidence and an expanding dealership network helped attract buyers to its electrified models.
"Malaysia's appetite for xEV vehicles continues to grow as evidenced by the strong demand for Pro-Net's range of Proton e.Mas products," he said.
Proton also recorded a monthly export high of 2,610 units in October, taking YTD exports of Proton and Geely models to 9,980 units, more than double the previous year's volume.
Abdul Rashid said export growth supported higher parts orders, better production utilisation and economies of scale.
He added that the segment was expected to contribute a larger share of group sales in the coming years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IOI Corp, TNB unit team up for 500MW solar project in Bahau
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Corp Bhd's wholly owned Luminous Aspect Sdn Bhd has partnered with Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) subsidiary to develop a 500-megawatt (MW) solar project in Negri Sembilan.
The project involves a 500MWac solar photovoltaic facility integrated with a 250MW/1,000MWh battery energy storage system.
IOI said Luminous had entered into a joint venture and shareholders' agreement with TNB Renewables Sdn Bhd (TRe) and CSP 500MW Sdn Bhd today.
The project marks IOI's first large-scale renewable energy development under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme.
TRe will hold a 70 per cent stake in Bahau Energy Ventures Sdn Bhd, the renewable energy development company.
Luminous and the consortium of small and medium enterprises will hold 25 per cent and five per cent respectively.
The development will be undertaken on 526.09 hectares of land in Bahau following a long-term land lease agreement between the development company and IOI.
The project will be supported by TNB's long-term renewable energy offtake agreement with Singapore-based DayOne Data Centres Ltd.
DayOne is expected to procure up to 500MWac of renewable energy over 21 years for its data centre operations in Malaysia.
IOI group managing director and chief executive Datuk Lee Yeow Chor said the partnership will provide the group with an opportunity to participate in one of the country's largest solar and energy storage projects.
"Supported by an offtake agreement with a reputable data centre company, we are optimistic that the project will yield stable long-term recurring income for IOI, both as a shareholder in the RED and as the lessor of the project site," he said.
He said the partnership also aligns with IOI's five-year strategic roadmap (2025-2029) to expand its renewable energy business portfolio.
The group's renewable energy initiatives include palm wood manufacturing and the processing of paper pulp from empty fruit bunch fibres.

Title: Govt has settled RM20.71bil in tax refunds as of Oct 31
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has refunded RM20.71 billion in excess tax payments involving 3.65 million taxpayers as of Oct 31.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said RM6.84 billion of the total was refunded to 3.4 million individual taxpayers.
"Meanwhile, RM13.036 billion was refunded to 206,234 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
"In processing these refunds, the government has prioritised tax overpayment reimbursements for individuals and MSMEs," he said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said, in line with this approach, the number of taxpayers with excess tax payments had been reduced by nearly half, from one million in December last year to 550,000 as at Oct 30 this year.
"The government remains committed to ensuring that all outstanding refunds are fully settled as soon as possible, as part of efforts to enhance tax administration efficiency and safeguard the rights of taxpayers, in alignment with the Madani government's fiscal reform agenda."
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said unclaimed money stood at RM14 billion as at Sept 30.
He said a lack of public awareness and knowledge about the existence of such funds and the right to claim them was among the main factors contributing to the accumulation of unclaimed money.
"Other factors include difficulties in locating the owners of these funds, often because contact information, such as addresses and telephone numbers, may be inaccurate or outdated.
"In many cases, owners are simply unaware that money is still owed to them by various entities or companies. Where the original owner has passed away, their heirs or estate administrators may also be unaware that such unclaimed funds exist.
"Furthermore, heirs or representatives often face challenges in providing the necessary documentation to prove their entitlement.
"Additionally, some owners have yet to claim their unclaimed money despite being aware of its existence due to personal reasons or time constraints," he said.
He said the government had implemented several measures to streamline the process of returning unclaimed money to its rightful owners, including those living in rural areas.
"Through the eGUMIS portal, the Accountant General's Department has made it easier for the public to check for and claim unclaimed money online.
"This system enhances the efficiency of managing unclaimed funds, ensuring that money belonging to individuals or organisations can be returned to its rightful owners quickly, easily and free of charge."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Global oil price volatility: Govt sticking to targeted subsidies to protect Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is maintaining its RM40 billion fuel subsidy commitment under the 2027 Budget to shield Malaysians from global oil price volatility and curb subsidy leakages.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the government remained committed to targeted subsidies to protect the people from rising global prices while ensuring that assistance reached the intended beneficiaries.
He said economists, including from the International Monetary Fund and local experts, had proposed setting fuel and electricity prices according to market rates for all consumers, with cash assistance provided only to the poor.
"The government does not agree with this approach. We remain committed to continuing targeted subsidies to protect the people from rising global prices, while curbing leakages caused by smuggling and ensuring that subsidy benefits do not fall into the hands of non-citizens.
"Therefore, this commitment of nearly RM40 billion is necessary to protect the people," he said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in Dewan Rakyat today.
Amir Hamzah said, through Budi Madani, Malaysians continued to enjoy subsidised RON95 petrol of up to 300 litres at RM1.99 per litre, compared with the actual market price of RM4.42 per litre.
Subsidised diesel of up to 400 litres was available at RM2.10 per litre, compared with the actual market price of RM5.27 per litre.
Looking ahead to next year, he said there was still no certainty that the conflict in the Middle East would ease or that oil prices would return to stable levels.
"Therefore, the government must be prepared for all eventualities and make every possible effort to ensure that the people remain protected."
On Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara), Amir Hamzah said that, as at Oct 31, a total of RM12 billion had been channelled to eligible recipients.
"Nearly nine million recipients had used Sara, recording RM6.15 billion in transactions, representing a utilisation rate of 99.7 per cent.
"Meanwhile, Sara for All had been used by 20.6 million recipients, or 92 per cent of eligible users, with total transactions exceeding RM1.95 billion."
On calls to reintroduce loan exemptions for students graduating with first-class honours from private higher education institutions, he said the government and the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) would study the proposal in line with the principle of targeted assistance.
"This is to ensure that PTPTN's funds remain sustainable for future generations of graduates."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UiTM to enrol first batch of Quantum Technology students next year
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) is expected to enrol its first batch of students in Quantum Technology next year.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said a Department of Quantum Technology would first be established to prepare the country for developments in the field.
"We will establish the department first. I think student enrolment could begin next year, in the next semester.
"Initially, training will be provided for teaching staff. Lecturers will be sent to pursue master's or doctoral studies, or attend short-term courses, so that those with backgrounds in information technology (IT) and digital technology can lead the department and faculty," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the Apa Khabar Mahasiswa? (Patriotisme Diperkasa bersama Azh@UiTM 2026) programme at UiTM's Alor Gajah campus in Melaka here today.
Also present was Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
Zahid said the government had allocated funds to UiTM to facilitate the establishment of the department, as quantum technology was among the emerging fields that warranted the country's attention.
He said the move was aimed at ensuring Malaysia kept pace with developments in emerging technologies, particularly in research and development.
"I believe technology is the new currency, and those in this field represent the new talent that will drive the country's technological advancement.
"We should be creators of new technologies, not merely participants in their development," he said.
He also expressed confidence that UiTM could identify lecturers with backgrounds in IT and digital technology to pursue further studies in quantum technology.
He said the initiative was important to develop a pool of academic staff capable of leading the field.
The media had earlier reported that UiTM was proposing to establish a Department of Quantum Technology by next year to produce more local experts in the emerging field.
Zahid was quoted as saying that the initiative was important to ensure Malaysia kept pace with developed countries, which were making rapid advances in quantum technology.

Title: Smoke from faulty air-conditioner triggers alarm at Johor hospital's pathology lab
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A faulty air-conditioning unit triggered a smoke scare at the Sultanah Aminah Hospital' s pathology laboratory here today.
Fire and Rescue Department operation commander Amirudin Mohamad said 12 firefighters from the Larkin station arrived at 4.07pm, eight minutes after the emergency call was placed.
Checks on the fourth floor of the building traced the smoke to damaged equipment inside an air-handling unit (AHU) room.
The team found no fire and did not carry out any extinguishing operation.
The building's maintenance team was contacted and the matter was handed over to them for further action.
The operation ended at 5.05pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cooperative manager pleads guilty to cheating by using fake documents for loan
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A cooperative manager pleaded guilty at the Sessions court here today to cheating a man with false supporting documents for a personal financing application four years ago.
Ku Siti Zulaikha Mohamed Zakkariya, 39, entered the plea after the alternative charge was read out before judge N. Kanageswari.
She was accused of dishonestly inducing Ibrahim Ali, 61, to believe that details in supporting documents submitted for the financing application were genuine, when they allegedly contained false information.
The offence was allegedly committed at the district government officers' cooperative (KOOPJB) office in Bangunan Kerjasama, Jalan Dhoby, here, on Sept 23, 2022.
She was charged under Section 417 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to five years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission prosecuting officer Fazal Lisam Abidin proposed bail of RM10,000 with one local surety pending the next court date.
Defence lawyer Azlan Bohari sought a lower bail amount, saying his client was still employed as a cooperative manager earning RM4,000 a month and had five children, three of whom were still schooling.
The court allowed bail at RM5,000 with one surety and fixed Nov 17 for the submission of the facts of the case and sentencing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Students' political views should be welcomed, as long as 3R is not involved
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Universities should not take disciplinary action against students for holding differing political views and beliefs, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said such differences should be welcomed, provided they did not touch on issues involving religion, royalty and race (3R).
"If students simply hold differing opinions and express their views, I believe those views should be welcomed rather than having legal action taken against them, unless they touch on 3R issues.
"The country's laws are very clear on such matters. Apart from that, universities should not take disciplinary action against students simply because they hold differing opinions and political beliefs," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the Apa Khabar Mahasiswa? (Patriotisme Diperkasa bersama Azh@UiTM 2026) programme at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Melaka's Alor Gajah campus here today.
Also present was Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
Zahid said the new law that would replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) would not restrict student activities.
However, he stressed that students would remain subject to the country's laws, including criminal laws.
"The new law will have a different name, but it will not involve students. It will cover university administration, academic matters, governance and the selection of senate members.
"This also includes the appointment of university management personnel, such as vice-chancellors and deputy vice-chancellors.
"However, students will remain subject to existing laws, including criminal laws," he said.
Earlier, in response to a student's question on freedom of expression among the younger generation, Zahid said students were free to express their ideas and views as long as they did not touch on 3R issues.
He said freedom of expression should be accompanied by courtesy and decorum when addressing differences of opinion.
"We can have differing opinions, but we must uphold proper conduct. We must observe courtesy and decorum when dealing with differences of opinion," he said.
It was previously reported that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in his presidential policy speech at the 2026 National PKR Congress in Melaka, announced that the government would abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit eases against greenback amid AI investment pullback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit eased against the US dollar on Tuesday amid a pullback in global artificial intelligence (AI)-related trades and investments.
At 6pm, the local note slipped to 4.0735/0775 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0695/0735.
SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the ringgit's weakness was largely driven by broader risk aversion, particularly as investors unwound AI-related investments.
He said Malaysia has been a major beneficiary of the global AI investment boom, particularly through its semiconductor industry and technology-related investment flows.
"The trouble is that this relationship cuts both ways. When investors start pulling back from the AI trade, the ringgit can come under pressure even when the broader US dollar is weakening.
"Therefore, the ringgit is getting caught up in the broader unwinding of the AI trade, and that may remain the bigger influence in the near term," he told Bernama.
Similarly, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit traded within a narrow range against the greenback as traders and investors weighed concerns over a potential AI investment bubble, the upcoming US midterm elections and Friday's US jobs data.
"On the AI investment bubble, there seem to be mixed signals among Wall Street firms at a conference in Hong Kong today.
"Some argued that AI infrastructure may have gone overboard, but others pointed to the potential benefits to the economy. Reversing risk appetite in the AI space could mean missing an opportunity to record further gains in investment returns," he said.
Mohd Afzanizam also noted that Brent crude oil prices rose 1.94 per cent to US$106.80 per barrel, as concerns over a possible renewed US attack on Iran following the US midterm elections remained a source of market uncertainty.
"Hence, overall, market sentiments are effectively guarded as there are a lot of moving parts that could easily tilt the balance of risk," he added.
Against major currencies, the ringgit traded mostly firmer.
The ringgit was marginally higher against the Japanese yen to 2.5762/5789 from 2.5766/5793 at Monday's close, inched up versus the euro to 4.5587/5631 from 4.5652/5697, but edged down vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4658/4712 from 5.4621/4675, previously.
The ringgit was mostly lower against its Asean peers.
It slipped versus the baht to 12.0696/0858 from 12.0496/0661 yesterday, inched down against the rupiah to 224.3/224.6 from 224.1/224.4, and fell vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.42/6.43 from 6.39/6.41 previously.
However, it rose against the Singapore dollar to 3.1807/1841 from the previous close of 3.1825/1862.

Title: Bridging rural digital skills gap with AI, digital training
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For some farmers, fishermen and small business owners in Muar, preparing for Malaysia's artificial intelligence (AI) future begins with learning how to set up an email account, use Microsoft Word and work with Excel spreadsheets.
The digital skills gap remains evident between rural and urban communities. In 2025, 83.6 per cent of rural households had access to a computer, compared with 95.3 per cent of urban households.
The disparity is also reflected in programming skills among computer users aged 15 to 24, with 34.1 per cent of rural users reporting coding skills compared with 56.3 per cent in urban areas, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia's ICT Use and Access by Individuals and Households Survey Report 2025.
A community-based initiative launched on Oct 28 aims to address this gap by equipping residents with essential digital skills before introducing them to AI, programming and game development.
The Program Kemahiran Digital, Pengaturcaraan dan Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) Muar was launched by Sungai Balang assemblyman Selamat Takim at the Ruang Daya Cipta (RDC) Centre in Sungai Balang.
[[nid:1569976]]
Funded by Microsoft, the programme aims to improve digital and AI literacy among local communities, including entrepreneurs who want to use technology to improve their businesses.
It was developed by YouthLabs Social Hub founder Kamariah Shakirin Mustafa, who brought together the programme partners and co-designed the initiative with RDC Centre programme manager Tok Mohd 'Adli Othman and Sungai Gersik village head Tok Syahroni Dulah Hussein.
Kamariah said the decision to introduce basic digital skills training came after discussions with the village leaders revealed that many residents had never created an email account or used applications such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
She said the programme was therefore structured to ensure participants could build their confidence with basic digital tools before progressing to more advanced technology.
"If Malaysia is to become an AI nation, rural communities need to come along too.
"Everyone has a different starting point, so we begin with the basics. We want people to see AI as a tool they understand and use with purpose, not something to fear or a shortcut that replaces their own thinking," she said.
For local entrepreneur Siti Roshanisa, who sells kerepek and tempeh in Kampung Parit Kemang, the training offers an opportunity to improve the way she manages her business.
"I do my stock taking by hand in a ledger. I want to learn Excel so I can keep track of my stock properly, and learn how AI can help my business do better," she said.
The first cohort, comprising 10 local entrepreneurs, completed training in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint on Oct 29.
The training was conducted by Nusantara Software, with participants scheduled to undergo Microsoft AI training in early November, delivered by Biji Biji, a Microsoft partner.
Participants will receive certificates jointly issued by Microsoft and the programme partners upon completing the AI training.
From November, a separate training component conducted by Nusantara Software and YouthLabs Social Hub will introduce young people to coding and game development, alongside AI-assisted learning for primary and secondary school pupils.
Through Nusantara Software's learning platform, pupils will be able to strengthen their understanding of school subjects with the help of technology.
Computers are provided at the RDC Centre, ensuring participants can access the training even if they do not own a computer at home.
Kamariah said the youth component was designed to encourage young people to move beyond consuming digital content and explore opportunities to create their own.
"Many young people here love e-sports. We want them to go from playing games to making them, perhaps one day build a career from what they create, and dream about where that could take them," she said.
Selamat said Johor's growing importance as a destination for AI investment made it essential for local communities to develop the skills needed to participate in the digital economy.
"Johor has become a key destination for AI investment, and many foreign investors have invested here.
"Our community must become more tech-savvy so that we benefit too, and our younger generation must learn about AI. I hope everyone gains as much as they can from this programme as we move further towards a digital economy," he said.
The programme is designed to continue beyond its launch, with each cohort limited to 10 participants to match the number of computers available at the RDC Centre.
A new cohort will begin every month, while local trainers will also be trained to ensure the community can sustain the initiative and extend digital skills training to more residents.
YouthLabs Social Hub also plans to collaborate with Southern Volunteers Daerah Muar, as well as Penghulu and village heads across Muar, to reach more young people and communities.
Under the partnership, Nusantara Software provides trainers and learning platforms for coding, game development and AI-assisted learning, while the RDC Centre supplies the venue and equipment.
The Community Development Department (Kemas) and local community leaders will assist in identifying and bringing in participants.
The programme is open to residents of Muar and surrounding areas. Participants below 18 must obtain parental or guardian consent to attend the sessions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yinson GreenTech taps carbon credit market via Saxon Renewables pact
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson GreenTech has partnered with Saxon Renewables to generate verified carbon credits from eligible electric vehicle (EV) activities.
The carbon programme is registered under Verra's Verified Carbon Standard (VCS).
The partnership follows the signing of a participation agreement allowing Yinson GreenTech to participate in EVolve, a carbon programme that combines multiple EV charging infrastructures under a single project.
Registered under Verra's VCS in November 2025, EVolve enables eligible charging infrastructure to generate carbon credits, subject to verification requirements.
Yinson GreenTech EV charging and leasing managing director Kelvin Soon said the partnership will help translate emissions reductions from electric mobility into measurable climate value.
"By participating in Saxon Renewables' EVolve programme, we can channel this value into a stronger charging network and better fleet electrification solutions to our customers," he said in a statement.
The collaboration will focus on integrating eligible charging infrastructure into the programme, strengthening data monitoring systems for independent verification and progressing towards carbon credit issuance.
Yinson GreenTech plans to expand charging access and fleet electrification while exploring the programme's application across its wider electric mobility portfolio.
Saxon Renewables managing director Reik Ong said the partnership was an important step in demonstrating the role of carbon markets in accelerating clean technology adoption in Malaysia and the region.
Saxon Renewables brings carbon project development experience across Asia, while Yinson GreenTech contributes its operational EV network to support the generation of carbon credits backed by verifiable data.
The partnership is the first technology-based carbon project advanced under Yinson's Carbon Project Framework.
The framework guides the group's selection of carbon opportunities and partners based on integrity, readiness and long-term value creation.

Title: FashionValet investment funds cannot be used to pay dividends, court told [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Investment funds channelled into FashionValet Sdn Bhd could not be used to pay dividends to any party, including the company's shareholders, the Sessions Court heard today.
Corporate lawyer Anne Wong Wai Yee said this was stipulated in the Shareholders' Agreement signed on March 5, 2018, between the e-commerce and fashion retail company and six investment-related companies.
She said she was responsible for preparing the draft agreement.
The six companies were Proven Holding Sdn Bhd, My E.G. Capital Sdn Bhd, Transasia E-Commerce Inc., Start Today Co. Ltd., Reussi Sdn Bhd and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd.
"FashionValet was also not allowed to enter into any agreement or understanding with related parties worth RM50,000 or more within a year without the approval of a majority of its board of directors.
"Such approval also had to be obtained from directors appointed by Start Today Co Ltd and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd.
"There was no provision allowing investment funds to be used for dividend payments to any party, including FashionValet's shareholders," she said.
Wong was reading her witness statement during the trial of former FashionValet directors Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar.
They are facing criminal breach of trust charges involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah Nasional Bhd and Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB).
Wong, the sixth prosecution witness, said the agreement also restricted the use of investment funds to specific purposes, including technology development, stores and warehouses, as well as products and brands.
She said the couple and the six companies had also entered into a deed of adherence with PNB on June 4, 2018.
On Dec 5, 2024, Vivy, 38, and Fadzarudin, 37, pleaded not guilty to jointly committing criminal breach of trust involving RM8 million belonging to Khazanah and PNB.
They were accused of making an RM8 million payment from FashionValet's bank account to 30 Maple Sdn Bhd without the company's board approval.
The offence was allegedly committed at Public Bank Berhad's Bukit Damansara branch here on Aug 21, 2018.
They were charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which provides for imprisonment of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The couple also pleaded not guilty to an alternative charge of dishonestly misappropriating RM8 million belonging to FashionValet, involving the same funds, date and location.
The alternative charge was framed under Section 403 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between six months and five years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The trial before judge Rosli Ahmad continues on Nov 20.

Title: RHB partners MEOA to boost plantation productivity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd has partnered with the Malaysian Estate Owners' Association (MEOA) to promote sustainable investment and improve productivity in the plantation sector.
The two-year partnership will provide financing solutions, industry engagement and technical support to help plantation operators adopt sustainable practices and strengthen business resilience.
RHB group chief sustainability officer Angus Salim Amran said closer cooperation between financial institutions and industry players was needed to accelerate the sector's sustainability transition.
"This transition requires purposeful integration between financial institutions and industry to further a robust sustainability ecosystem.
"Through this pioneering RHB and MEOA partnership, we aspire to collectively facilitate practical solutions and unlock opportunities to support long-term business resilience," he said in a statement.
The partnership was formalised through a memorandum of understanding witnessed by Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad at MEOA's 95th anniversary gala dinner 2026 last week.
Both parties will support investments in oil palm replanting, renewable energy, energy efficiency, decarbonisation, workers' welfare and circular economy initiatives.
These include solar photovoltaic systems, biogas facilities, energy-efficient machinery, methane capture projects and improvements to workers' housing and welfare.
The collaboration will also include workshops and industry engagements to help estate owners understand sustainable and transition financing, meet regulatory requirements and manage climate-related risks.
MEOA president Ahmad Zachry Anifah Aman said the partnership will enable the association to share members' operational experience with RHB while helping estate owners identify suitable financing and implementation options.
MEOA has 163 members representing about 1.2 million hectares of oil palm and rubber estates nationwide.
The partnership also supports RHB's sustainable finance agenda under its PROGRESS27 strategy.
To date, the group has mobilised RM71 billion in sustainable financial services, against its RM90 billion target by 2027.

Title: UK PM to raise debt reset and trade at Commonwealth summit
Article:
ST JOHN'S: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will set out his vision for a debt reset and stronger trade with Commonwealth countries at a summit on Tuesday that is likely to hear calls for slavery reparations.
Burnham will join King Charles and leaders from the Commonwealth's 56 member states in Antigua and Barbuda, where he will argue that the organisation can play a bigger role in tackling global challenges including climate change, economic growth and security.
Charles, symbolic head of the grouping, has during a week-long visit to the Caribbean sought to acknowledge "the great suffering and injustices of the past" without going so far as to issue a formal apology for slavery, sticking with the British government's long-term approach.
But Burnham said at the weekend he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, although not the payment of reparations.
His spokesman said on Monday that talks would begin in Antigua on what shape any apology could take.
"We think it's right that a formal apology is discussed properly with the countries and communities most affected, rather than simply deciding unilaterally what form it should take," the spokesman said.
Both Burnham and the king are, however, likely to stress what more the Commonwealth, which comprises mostly former British colonies and encompasses some 2.7 billion people, can do to strengthen the smaller members.
Burnham's office said around half of developing countries struggling with debt are in the Commonwealth, with rising global interest rates exacerbating the pressure they face.
Work to stop those countries from being trapped in debt spirals must include donors outside the G7 club of rich economies, as well as the private sector, Burnham will say on Tuesday.
He will also announce taskforces to increase investment in Commonwealth countries' critical mineral industries and reduce barriers to trade, along with £40 million (US$54 million) of investments into critical infrastructure in the Caribbean over the next three years.
The king will open the summit on Tuesday and, while he is expected to mention slavery, he will also focus on bringing people together to tackle the challenges of today.
"His Majesty's most significant contribution has been helping to connect leaders, institutions and investors ... around shared areas of interest and concern," a palace spokesperson said.
That is unlikely to appease some member countries, including CARICOM, the Caribbean Community, a group of 23 member and associate member states including the Bahamas, Barbados and Jamaica, which has been pushing for reparations to be on the meeting's agenda.
From the 15th to the 19th century, at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery ​by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million people across the Atlantic, making it one of the biggest slave-trading nations, according to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database.

Title: GWM WEY G9 hybrid: Luxury without the plug
Article:
THE self-charging hybrid brings a more accessible entry point to GWM's premium MPV range, pairing all-wheel drive with a cabin designed around passenger comfort.
The recent climb towards Genting Highlands provided an appropriate setting to put the GWM WEY G9 Hi4 HEV through its paces, with the media drive taking in trunk roads and a stretch of Karak Highway before returning to Genting Awana.
Starting from Bamboo Hills in Segambut, the convoy headed directly to Genting Awana for a briefing before resuming the drive.
The subsequent 40-minute session included driver changes at three designated areas, offering participants the opportunity to experience the MPV from behind the wheel.
The drive was relatively short, but the route provided a mix of road conditions against which to consider the WEY G9's positioning as a luxury people-mover that does not require owners to plug in to benefit from electrification.
Hybrid Power, Without Charging Stops
Priced at RM249,800, the WEY G9 Hi4 HEV is RM20,000 cheaper than its plug-in hybrid (PHEV) sibling.
The distinction is important. While the PHEV offers a larger battery and an electric-only driving capability, the HEV is designed for buyers who prefer the convenience of a conventional petrol-powered vehicle, supplemented by electric assistance.
Under the bonnet is a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine paired with two electric motors, a 1.67kWh battery and a four-speed dedicated hybrid transmission.
The combination produces a claimed system output of 358PS and 782Nm of torque, delivered through GWM's intelligent Hi4 all-wheel-drive system.
GWM claims a zero-to-100km/h acceleration time of 7.5 seconds, fuel consumption of 6.5 litres per 100km under the NEDC test cycle and a combined driving range of up to 845km.
The figures suggest a useful balance between performance and long-distance usability for a vehicle designed to carry seven people.
However, the short media drive was not sufficient to establish real-world fuel consumption, particularly under sustained climbing or with a full passenger load.
The HEV's main appeal is straightforward. Drivers can enjoy the benefits of a hybrid powertrain without having to plan journeys around charging stops or install a home charger.
A Cabin Built Around Passengers
At 5,050mm long, 1,985mm wide and 1,900mm tall, the WEY G9 has substantial road presence.
Its 3,085mm wheelbase also provides the foundation for a three-row cabin arranged in a 2+2+3 configuration.
The second row is the centrepiece, with captain seats featuring electric leg rests, ventilation and massage functions, which add a touch of first-class comfort for passengers on longer journeys.
The front seats also offer electric adjustment and ventilation, while the first two rows are upholstered in Nappa leather.
For families undertaking longer journeys, or businesses transporting clients, the emphasis is clearly on making time spent in the vehicle more comfortable rather than treating the MPV simply as a means of getting from one destination to another.
Practicality has not been overlooked. The third row can be folded to increase luggage capacity, while powered sliding doors and a powered tailgate simplify access in tighter parking spaces.
The technology package includes a 14.6-inch infotainment touchscreen, a 12.3-inch digital instrument display, a head-up display, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and a 21-speaker sound system.
Acoustic glass and active noise cancellation are intended to reduce cabin noise, an important consideration on faster highway stretches.
The Price Of Going Premium
The WEY G9 Hi4 HEV's equipment list is extensive for a vehicle below RM250,000, although buyers should look beyond the headline specifications when assessing its value.
Its large dimensions may make manoeuvring in confined urban spaces more demanding than in a conventional family SUV.
Driver-assistance systems, including adaptive cruise control, lane-centre keeping and blind-spot detection, help support the driving task, but do not remove the need for careful attention.
The HEV also gives up some of the PHEV's flexibility. Its small battery is designed to support the hybrid system rather than provide a meaningful electric-only driving range.
Buyers with convenient home charging who regularly make short journeys may therefore find the more expensive PHEV a better fit.
For those who prioritise convenience, however, the HEV presents a different proposition: electrified performance without a change in refuelling habits.
GWM offers a six-year unlimited-mileage vehicle warranty and an eight-year or 180,000km warranty for the high-voltage battery, electric drive motor and motor control unit, alongside five years of free scheduled servicing.
The Genting Awana drive offered an introduction to the WEY G9 Hi4 HEV rather than a definitive verdict on its long-distance efficiency or ride comfort.
Even so, its combination of a self-charging hybrid system, all-wheel drive and a well-equipped seven-seat cabin gives it a clear target audience.
For buyers considering a luxury MPV but reluctant to depend on charging infrastructure, the WEY G9 Hi4 HEV makes a case for hybrid convenience at a lower entry price.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khazanah Wolfson Press Fellows mentor next generation of communicators
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) communications students were given an insight into newsroom operations today, thanks to four Khazanah Wolfson Press Fellows.
They were part of day-long programme led by
Business Times
editor Muhammed Ahmad Hamdan,
New Straits Times
specialist writer Iylia Marsya Iskandar,
Borneo Post
business reporter James Wong and Astro Awani journalist Shafizan Johari.
The Khazanah Residency Programme (KRP) "POV: Your Work in Comms", was hosted by IIUM's Department of Communication, Abdul Hamid Abu Sulayman Kulliyyah of Islamic Revealed Knowledge and Human Sciences (AHAS KIRKHS), with more than 70 students from the department taking part.
AHAS KIRHS dean Professor Dr Hafiz Zakariya thanked Khazanah Nasional Bhd for choosing the department for the programme, saying the engagement with industry practitioners allowed students to understand how academic knowledge is applied in the real world.
"We deeply appreciate Khazanah's commitment to engaging with and nurturing the next generation of communication professionals who are here today.
"Meaningful engagement with industry professionals allows students to understand how this knowledge is applied in the real world," he said in his welcoming remarks.
Khazanah executive director and head of group sustainability and advocacy Datuk Shahira Ahmed Bazari urged students to uphold ethical and accountable communication as they prepare to enter the industry.
"You have a strong responsibility to ensure that what you communicate externally is guided by good ethics and accountability," she said, addressing the students.
She urged them to make full use of the opportunity to learn from the industry practitioners and mentors during the programme.
The mentors also shared insights from their professional experiences and guided students through practical exercises designed to expose them to the realities of journalism and communications work.
Nur Hidayah Hasan, 24, said the programme's full-day activities left her "more prepared" to enter the journalism field.
"I gained a clearer understanding of the importance of accuracy, timeliness and reporting facts as they are," the communications student specialising in integrated media journalism said, recalling the activity which required students to assess a simulated media crisis before developing their news reports.
Meanwhile, Nur Syakirah Iman Mohd Shafique, who specialises in strategic communications, found herself putting theories learnt in class into practice while managing a simulated crisis which was part of the programme.
"It was challenging to balance being transparent with protecting the organisation's reputation, but that made the experience more realistic," the 24-year-old said.
Established in 2013, the Khazanah Residency Programme (KRP) aims to develop Malaysian talent in the media and creative sectors through international exposure and professional immersion.
One of KRP's initiatives, the Khazanah Wolfson Press Fellowship, provides journalists with opportunities to broaden their knowledge and skills through international learning experiences, with fellows sharing their expertise with the wider media community upon their return.
The fellows' involvement as mentors also reflected the fellowship's emphasis on sharing knowledge and contributing to the development of the next generation of media professionals.

Title: The Great Gap: Why passenger cars sales are growing while commercial vehicle sales are shrinking
Article:
THE latest set of statistics from the Malaysian Automotive Association (MAA) for September presents a stark - if concerning - contrast in the health of our automotive landscape.
While the industry celebrates total industry volume (TIV) comfortably clearing the 600,000- unit mark during the first nine months, growing four per cent year-on-year, a worrying trend is developing in the commercial vehicle market, it is shrinking.
Passenger vehicle sales rose sharply by 22 per cent year-on-year in September while commercial vehicle sales contracted by seven per cent for the month, dragging year-to-date performance down by a staggering 13 per cent to just 37,714 units.
The MAA attributed the slight month-on-month cooling to a "wait-and-see" approach ahead of the National Budget announcement.
However this obvious finger pointing of consumer hesitation ahead of a budget is far too convenient an excuse for a much deeper structural crisis, especially when you dig into the composition of those commercial numbers.
But for January and July when the commercial vehicle market surged, all other months have recorded reductions,
As for the two monthly anomalies, January's 15 per cent boost is totally expected as companies rush for early-year fleet delivery and fulfilment of December backlogs. July's high jump of 30 per cent sales of pick-up trucks was fuelled by the announcement of Budi Diesel subsidy scheme.
That July movement holds a lot of clues.
If you break down that 13 per cent year-to-date collapse in the commercial sector, the bleeding is heavily concentrated in the light commercial vehicle (LCV) and pick-up truck segments - precisely the essential workhorses relied upon by our small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
Small business owners operating delivery vans, logistics support, and rural service fleets find themselves caught in a severe financial squeeze.
Between strict diesel subsidy rationalisation, fluctuating fuel prices, and unpredictable global energy markets driven by Middle Eastern tensions, operating traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) workhorses has become a budgeting nightmare.
The numbers tell a punishing story. While eligible commercial fleets under controlled systems enjoy subsidised rates anchored around RM2.10 to RM2.15 per litre, unsubsidised retail diesel in Peninsular Malaysia has experienced violent market spikes, surging past the RM5.00-per-litre mark.
For micro-SMEs, sole proprietors, or sub-contractors operating pick-up trucks that fall through the cracks of rigid fleet card quotas, this creates an unmanageable financial chasm - more than doubling their fuel expenditure overnight.
Consider the math on the ground: a small logistics or service contractor running a workhorse pick-up or panel van over 4,000 kilometres a month burns roughly 400 litres of diesel.
At controlled baseline rates, that is an RM840 monthly fuel bill. When forced to swallow unsubsidised market peaks, that exact same monthly mileage skyrockets past RM2,000 out of pocket - an extra burden of over RM1,200 per vehicle, every single month.
When fuel traditionally accounts for up to 40 per cent of an SME's operating expenditure, and fixed-rate client contracts prevent them from passing these surging costs downstream, net operating margins are entirely obliterated.
Small businesses operating on a modest 10-15 per cent net profit margin can see their profitability wiped out by just two commercial units paying market-rate fuel.
Unsurprisingly, businesses have frozen capital expenditure. They simply aren't buying new pick-up trucks or panel vans because daily running costs and strict fuel caps are too volatile to forecast.
They are clinging onto aging, high-mileage diesel workhorses, trying to stretch every final kilometre out of dying engines.
On the other side of the showroom floor, however, private passenger buyers are enjoying a golden era.
A relentless wave of new electrified models - from affordable hybrids to accessible Chinese and local electric vehicles like the Proton e.Mas - has captured public imagination.
With home and public charging offering a fraction of petrol costs, individual motorists see passenger EVs as a logical escape valve from rising living expenses.
Yet, this highlights a glaring blind spot in our national transition: while private urban buyers enjoy an abundance of sub-RM150,000 options, commercial operators have been left high and dry.
Bound to traditional diesel engines with no viable, cost-effective alternatives in sight, small businesses are being squeezed from all directions.
If Malaysia's economic foundation is to remain stable, policy focus cannot remain fixated solely on private passenger cars in metropolitan hubs.
Policymakers must urgently recalibrate support systems - offering more realistic commercial diesel protections, safeguarding operating quotas for the micro-enterprises that keep our supply chains moving, and paving the way for affordable commercial electrification.
Without immediate relief and a clear, accessible transition pathway for SMEs, the widening gap between private motoring luxury and commercial fleet paralysis will ultimately translate into higher operational costs, tighter margins, and supply chain friction for the entire economy.

Title: Chery shifts global expansion into high gear
Article:
WUHU, China: Chery Automobile Co Ltd is shifting gears in its global expansion strategy, with locally manufactured vehicles set to account for more than half of overseas sales next year.
Executive vice president Zhang Guibing said the target reflects its shift from exporting cars to building a global manufacturing and technology ecosystem.
He said locally produced vehicles were expected to account for more than 50 per cent of overseas sales by end-2026, up from a projected average of more than 48 per cent.
The strategy includes expanding manufacturing, research and development (R&D) and supply chains in overseas markets, while strengthening partnerships with local businesses.
"We are not just going there to sell products. We are also creating jobs and cooperating with local technologies," he said at the 2026 Chery International User Summit.
Zhang said Chery planned to establish 26 local R&D centres, building on 16 already in operation, to develop products suited to different markets.
The company operates in more than 130 countries and has served 7.4 million customers, reflecting its growing international presence.
EXPORTS DRIVE GROWTH
Zhang said Chery's annual sales had doubled from about one million vehicles to two million within two years, while the company accounted for one in every four vehicles exported from China.
He said the Chinese automaker ranked ninth globally in the first half of 2026 before rising to fifth place in August, while its new energy vehicle (NEV) sales had more than doubled annually.
Beyond vehicle sales, Chery is expanding into artificial intelligence (AI), autonomous driving, robotics and green materials to improve manufacturing and develop new mobility services.
Separately, chairman Yin Tongyue said the company was transforming from a traditional carmaker into a high-tech industrial ecosystem, with AI reshaping its products, operations and business models.
The company has developed CheryMind, an enterprise AI model intended to support R&D, manufacturing, supply chain management and customer service.
It is also exploring applications across robotaxis, commercial vehicles, motorcycles, agricultural machinery and electric boats.
Yin said the company's Yaoguang 2035 strategy would integrate AI, computing power, hardware and software into vehicles, while extending its technological capabilities into other industries.
"Today, we use AI to redefine cars. We are moving towards machine and AI integration," he said at the 2026 Chery Global Innovation Conference on Oct 20.
He added that Chery wanted to strengthen its international brands through differentiated products rather than competing primarily on price.
MALAYSIA PLANT KEY
Malaysia is part of Chery's manufacturing expansion, with the company developing a RM2.2 billion Smart Auto Industrial Park in Lembah Beringin, Selangor.
Completed in June, the plant is expected to begin operations in the first quarter of 2027.
The facility is intended to strengthen local production, develop supply chains and support regional exports.
It is expected to initially produce 100,000 vehicles annually, with capacity scalable to 300,000 units.
Chery currently assembles vehicles at Sime Darby Bhd's Inokom Corp Sdn Bhd facility in Kulim, Kedah.
Since returning to Malaysia in 2023, the automaker has sold 55,800 vehicles across its four brands.
It became the country's fifth-largest automotive group in 2025, selling 31,646 vehicles and capturing a four per cent market share through its brands Chery, Omoda/Jaecoo, iCaur and Lepas.
Zhang said Chery was also seeking deeper cooperation with suppliers, with more than 90 per cent of the world's top 100 automotive suppliers working with the company.
He said collaboration with suppliers and even former competitors could accelerate technological development, improve efficiency and create opportunities across international markets.
NEW MODELS SHOWCASE TECHNOLOGY
Chery unveiled the all-new Tiggo 7 and Tiggo X7 sport utility vehicles (SUVs) at its brand night event on Oct 21, under the theme "Together. For Family".
The Tiggo 7 targets everyday family use, while the Tiggo X7 is positioned as a family-oriented SUV combining urban practicality with capabilities for different road conditions.
The all-new models have not yet been confirmed for the Malaysian market.
In Malaysia, the company offers the Tiggo 7 Pro, powered by a 1.6-litre turbocharged petrol engine, and the Tiggo 7 PHEV CSH, which combines a 1.5-litre petrol engine with an electric motor.

Title: Zahid denies sabotaging Madani government over Sabah, Sarawak projects [WATCH]
Article:
JASIN: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that he attempted to sabotage the Madani government over the status of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, maintained that his remarks on the suspension or cancellation of letters of acceptance for the projects were factual.
He added that he was prepared to produce official documents to prove his claims.
"I had no such intention (to sabotage the government). Whether the projects have been postponed or cancelled, the fact remains that there were instructions to cancel all SSTs that have been or are due to be issued.
"I have documentary evidence of the instructions. I can show it," he said to reporters after officiating the Mara Higher Education and TVET Tour 2026 programme here today.
Yesterday, Jelutong member of parliament RSN Rayer, while interjecting during a debate in the Dewan Rakyat, questioned Zahid's remarks concerning the cancellation of the rural development projects, describing them as an attempt to sabotage the Madani government.
